clue.text: A good deal at the auction sale?

definitions.meaning: a good deal, a great quantity
at an auction each numbered item put up for sale is a lot

explanation.definitionFit: A large amount is colloquially plenty or loads, and the items sold under the hammer at auctions are numbered lots.

clue.text: Helen's mother died in the field

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for died is placed within the word for field

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassy field in poetic usage
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A family history noting that Helen's mother perished out in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Helen of Troy was the daughter of Zeus and the mortal queen of Sparta, who was visited by the god in the form of a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Spartan queen seduced by Zeus as a swan bore Helen of Troy.

clue.text: Heel producing on inventory

definitions.meaning: of a ship, to heel is to lean over to one side
an inventory is an itemised catalogue of goods

explanation.surface: A shoe heel is somehow producing a stock inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leans to one side is said to heel or tilt, and a catalogue of items is an enumerated record.

clue.text: Meat which may be cooked in ovens

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters that follow are worked up into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A recipe note: this meat is the kind you might roast in ovens.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer flesh eaten as food is called by this name.

clue.text: A forecaster must look to the heavens

definitions.text: A forecaster must look to the heavens

parts.words: A forecaster must look to the heavens
parts.note: reads like a weather forecaster watching the sky, but the forecaster predicts the future from the stars and planets

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters have to keep an eye on the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A horoscope writer predicts people's fortunes by studying the positions of stars and planets.

clue.text: The beauty appears without wrinkles

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for appears goes around the other piece

parts.note: comes, as in arrives or shows up, means appears
lines on the face are wrinkles

explanation.surface: A beauty who shows up with no wrinkles at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but in its older sense it means 'outside', so the word for appears wraps around the wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractiveness of appearance in a person is called by this rather old-fashioned noun.

clue.text: Set apart for Easter-egg making

indicators.note: making here means the letters are made into a new word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Sorting chocolate so some is put aside for producing Easter eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate people or things and keep them isolated from others is to set them apart.

clue.text: Figure refuse should bring money

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so a figure
ash is the waste left after burning, so refuse

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a rubbish figure ought to fetch some money.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes and coins in hand are ready money.

clue.text: Perfectly happy just to read when camping

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or read carefully
tented describes someone housed under canvas, as when camping

explanation.surface: A camper perfectly happy just to sit and read in the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being satisfied and at ease with one's lot is being perfectly happy.

clue.text: Beginning to absorb the Left and that's very surprising

indicators.note: to absorb means the word for beginning takes the other letter into itself

parts.note: starting means beginning

explanation.surface: A politician starting to absorb the Left, which is a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing or alarming that makes one jump is very surprising.

clue.text: Degenerate rock-climber

indicators.note: in a down clue a climber goes upwards, so the word for rock is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A rock-climber who has gone to the bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock-climber' reads as one sportsman; split it: a TOR (a craggy hilltop) 'climbs', reading upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To decay or decompose is to degenerate, as fruit does when it goes off.

clue.text: No servicemen's standard

parts.note: taken as written
RM stands for the Royal Marines, British servicemen

explanation.surface: A complaint that servicemen are below standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A usual level or expected pattern is the standard against which things are judged.

clue.text: Desert animal

definitions.meaning: to desert one's friends or side is to inform on or abandon them

explanation.surface: Something living in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat who abandons his side is said to do this, and the long-tailed rodent is a familiar creature.

clue.text: A hole most may well find sickening

indicators.note: may well suggests the letters could quite possibly be found in some other order

explanation.surface: Most people would find a hole in something disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive and detestable is sickening.

clue.text: Temporarily providing for a hooligan in extremity? No, quite the reverse

indicators.note: in sets one piece inside the other
says the containment just described is the wrong way round, so the hooligan surrounds the extremity

parts.note: a lout is a rough, uncouth hooligan
an ending is an extremity, the end point of something

explanation.surface: A charity lending to a hooligan in dire straits, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally the hooligan would go inside the extremity; 'No, quite the reverse' flips the containment, so the extremity sits inside the hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing something over for a set period to be returned is providing it temporarily.

clue.text: Bond, given in welcome, set about the guys!

annotationWithheld.why: Bond, given in welcome, set about the guys! (9): MEN inside GREET gives GREMENT plus an A that no clue word supplies ('given' cannot be A); the clue as held looks short of a word such as 'a', and no source confirms it
annotationWithheld.clue: Bond, given in welcome, set about the guys!

clue.text: He's lit on a solution to the downfall

indicators.note: a solution is a dissolving or working out, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective has hit on the answer to someone's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' sounds like ruin but here means something falling down from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice falling from storm clouds is literally a downfall of precipitation.

clue.text: A woman writing articles in Spanish and French

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine definite article
la is the French feminine definite article

explanation.surface: A woman who writes pieces in Spanish and French.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, as of the jazz singer Fitzgerald.

clue.text: Merging in, aren't seen to get on board

indicators.note: merging means the letters are blended together into a new order

explanation.surface: Traffic merging in, apparently invisible, as people climb aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a railway carriage, as troops do, is to get on board.

clue.text: Need time to organise the place

parts.note: a want is a need or lack
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone who needs time to organise a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: WANTAGE is a market town in Oxfordshire, England, birthplace of King Alfred.
explanation.definitionFit: This English market town in Oxfordshire is a place on the map.

clue.text: Residential areas, as the egghead says

parts.note: read as egg-head, the head or first letter of the word egg
states means says or declares

explanation.surface: Housing developments, as described by an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual; split it into 'egg' and 'head', the first letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Housing developments built as a planned group of homes are residential areas.

clue.text: Wooden, sanctimonious, and heartless nurse

parts.note: pi is a short slang form of pious, so sanctimonious

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of nurse is removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A stiff, self-righteous, unfeeling nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture made of a softwood timber is wooden, the word used as an adjective.

clue.text: America backing the prodigal will hold things up

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation for America goes in reverse

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States, America
a prodigal is a wasteful spender

explanation.surface: America supporting the prodigal will stall progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold things up' suggests delay, but a garter belt holds stockings up.
explanation.definitionFit: A garter strap literally keeps stockings or socks raised, so it is a holder-up of things.

clue.text: Born in Greece a Hellene, evidently

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting inside the words a little further on

explanation.surface: Someone born in Greece is plainly a Hellene.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles the end of 'Hellene' and the start of 'evidently'.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word, used before a married woman's maiden name, means born.

clue.text: Dull floor-covering

definitions.meaning: a matt surface is dull, without shine
a rug or small piece of carpet covers the floor

explanation.surface: A drab rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-shiny finish is a variant spelling of matt, and a rug at the door is a small floor-covering.

clue.text: Only some in a guest-house make complaint

indicators.note: Only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Just a few guests at a boarding house grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'make complaint' as the definition, but the answer is a noun, an illness; 'make' is a link (some make, i.e. form, the answer).
explanation.definitionFit: A fever with fits of shivering, malarial in origin, is an illness, which is a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: Agreed on a cocktail as the non-alcoholic drink

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Friends settle on a cocktail but end up with a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy soft drink flavoured with citrus fruit is non-alcoholic.

clue.text: Entrance the spectators

definitions.meaning: a way in through a fence or wall is an entrance
the number of people attending a match is the crowd or attendance

explanation.surface: Delighting the onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged barrier is an entrance, and a football crowd figure is the attendance at the match.

clue.text: Insubstantial though sound nest

indicators.note: sound here signals that the word for nest is pronounced like the answer

parts.note: an eyrie is an eagle's nest

explanation.surface: Flimsy, though the nest is solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something light, delicate and lacking substance is insubstantial.

clue.text: Having set a spread, partakes of it

indicators.note: spread, as in scattered, means the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Having laid a feast, the host joins in.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking food from a meal is consuming it.

clue.text: A poet's hound

definitions.meaning: Leigh ... was an English Romantic poet and essayist
to hound is to pursue or chase relentlessly

explanation.surface: A poet's dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Leigh Hunt was a Romantic poet, and to hound a quarry is to chase it down.

clue.text: Choose to talk-they make one cross!

parts.note: to elect is to choose, especially by vote
to orate is to talk, making a speech

explanation.surface: Being told to choose and to speak makes someone angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry'; voters mark ballot papers with a cross (X).
explanation.definitionFit: Voters as a body mark their ballot papers with an X, so they make a cross.
